# SPE round 5 plan: invoice extraction

Round 5 tests P1. Config S is R with OCR cleanup skipped on two-column layouts. Q and R run again unchanged so S can be compared with both. Config P is retired. The eval set stays at the same 60 invoices.

**Defaults for details not in the pasted text:**
- The last requirement and disagreement IDs are not shown. I use R40 and D5 as stand-ins. When I write the files, I will renumber them to follow the last real IDs.
- The round 4 trial count is not shown. I default to 3 trials per invoice. If r04.yaml says otherwise, I will use the r04 count.
- Round 4 also had metrics other than field accuracy, such as PO mismatch flags. Those rows carry into r05.yaml at their round 4 measured values for Q and R. S copies Q's values for them, because no round 5 change targets them.

## Specify

The new invoices need reference fields from the AP lead, and only the user can arrange that. If the set changed in the same round as S, a move in field accuracy could come from either change. |
| P3: drop config P | Adopted | P trailed Q on every round 4 metric. Q is now the baseline. Dropping P frees its share of the trial budget for S. |

## Predict

The starting point is the round 4 measured value for each unchanged config. Each number moves only for the reason given in its Why.

| Metric (grader check) | Q | R | S | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field accuracy, all 60 (`field_match`) | 0.93 ± 0.02 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.93 ± 0.03 | Q and R are unchanged, so each starts at its r04 measured value. S skips cleanup on two-column layouts, which is where R lost fields. No measurement yet shows that cleanup helps any other invoices, so I predict S equals Q. |
| Line-item recall, two-column subset (`line_item_recall@two_column`) | 0.95 ± 0.04 | 0.65 ± 0.15 | 0.95 ± 0.04 | F9 found that cleanup drops line items on two-column layouts. S does not run cleanup on those invoices, so it should match Q. |

The values in rows 2 and 3 are my estimates, because round 4 did not report these subsets. The control gate will produce the r04 values for these rows. I will log those values next to the predictions and will not edit the predictions.

## Evaluate

### After approval

Each step ends with a local commit. Nothing is pushed.

1. **Specify.** Save the pasted text and "go again" word for word to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`. Append the round 5 requirement table to `spe/spec/spec.md`. Mark each "Proposed for round 5" row with its decision. Add D5 to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Write `spe/evals/fixtures/layout-tags.yaml`. Commit `spe(r05): specify`.
2. **Predict.** Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` from the Predict table. Commit `spe(r05): predict`.
3. **Build.** Add config S, with the layout check and the skip rule. Add the grader checks `line_item_recall@two_column`, `total_exact@scanned`, `cleanup_calls@two_column`, and `layout_tag_agreement`. Write `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js`. Commit `spe(r05): config S and grader checks`.

### Gates

The gates run in this order. If any gate fails, I halt and report.

1. **Grader selftest.** The reference fields, fed in as agent output, score 1.0 on every check. An empty output scores 0. Every invoice has a layout tag. The manifest hash matches r04.
2. **Control.** Regrade the r04 outputs for Q and R with the r05 grader. Field accuracy must come out at exactly 0.93 and 0.88, because the outputs and the scoring of this metric are unchanged.
3. **Dry run.** Run 3 invoices per config: one two-column, one scanned, and one digital single-column. The gate passes when all of the following hold:
   - S makes no cleanup call on the two-column invoice, and R makes at least one.
   - Every output matches the schema.
   - No reference field appears in any agent's context.
4. **Launch the Workflow.**

### Workflow arguments

```yaml
script: spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js
round: r05
configs: [Q, R, S]
invoices: r04 manifest (60 invoices)
trials_per_invoice: 3
layout_fixture: spe/evals/fixtures/layout-tags.yaml
predictions: spe/predictions/r05.yaml
budget_cap_usd: 100
```

### Cost (unmeasured estimate)

The run makes 540 agent calls (60 invoices × 3 configs × 3 trials), plus 9 calls for the dry run. I estimate about 20k input tokens and 2k output tokens per call, with more for R and S when cleanup runs. That comes to roughly $40 to $70. Round 4 also ran 3 configs, so the cost should be close to round 4's.

### Halt and stop

- I halt and report if any of these happen: the $100 budget cap is reached, the grader selftest fails, the control does not reproduce r04, or a reference field leaks into an agent's context.
- The 3-rounds-matched stop rule does not apply yet, because R missed in round 4.

### Learn (after the run)

1. Append the r05 rows to `spe/prediction-log.md`, with hit or miss for each cell. Commit `spe(r05): evaluate`.
2. Update F9 in `spe/failures.md`. Mark it fixed if S's two-column line-item recall lands inside its band. Otherwise, keep it open and add the new evidence. Log any new failure type as F10 onward.
3. Write a "Proposed for round 6" table in spec.md. Note there that D5 is still open for the user to decide. Commit `spe(r05): learn`.
